claims.evidence: Witness report shows a used diesel/industrial engine assembly with no readable brand/model markings visible; no make/model plate details were captured.
No documentation, markings, or provenance details were shown in the witness observations.
Witness report includes only visual condition; it does not show running, starting, smoke level, or output/power test results.
No audio/recording or running test observation is included in the witness report.
No hour meter reading or maintenance log is shown; no model plate details are readable.
No inspection evidence (gasket condition, fastener tamper marks, internal photos) is provided in the witness report.

risks.risk: Engine may not actually be the claimed make/model (Detroit 671) or may be a different industrial diesel; wrong parts compatibility affects value and repair cost.
risks.proof: Clear close-up photo of the engine make/model plate (or stamped ID) and/or a visible engine serial number; include a shot showing the plate text.
risks.if_unproven: Price as an unidentified used diesel/industrial engine assembly (worst-case parts compatibility), not as a verified Detroit 671.

risks.risk: Not proven to run: starting/compression/combustion issues, worn bearings, or injector problems could exist despite appearance.
risks.proof: Video clip of cold start and steady running (showing RPM stability), plus a short clip of load/output test if available.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not working/unknown running condition (worst-case), with buyer assuming overhaul risk.

risks.risk: Internal wear not visible: cylinder head/crankshaft/bearings may be worn even if externally dusty/dirty.
risks.proof: Compression test results and/or borescope inspection clip; also show any service records or teardown evidence if claimed 'never opened'.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming possible major wear (overhaul risk) rather than 'low mileage'.

risks.risk: Leaks and seal/gasket condition unknown (oil/coolant/fuel). External dirt can hide fresh leaks.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of suspected leak points (base, valve cover area, hoses, fittings) and a short run clip showing no drips/smoke.
risks.if_unproven: Price as having unknown leak status; treat as needing inspection and possible reseal.

risks.risk: Completeness/accessories uncertain: starter, turbo (if any), injectors, radiator/cooling parts, and mounting hardware may be missing.
risks.proof: Inventory photo list: show each accessory separately (starter, alternator, turbo if present, injectors, cooling components) and confirm what is included.
risks.if_unproven: Price as incomplete/unknown accessories (worst-case missing key components).

risks.risk: Marine-specific configuration may be different from generic industrial setup (cooling, exhaust, wiring harness, controls).
risks.proof: Photos of marine-specific components/controls and wiring harness connections; show the full unit layout (not just engine).
risks.if_unproven: Price as generic industrial diesel engine assembly unless marine configuration is clearly shown.

proof_requests: Send a clear close-up photo of the engine make/model plate and serial number (text readable).
Provide a video of the engine starting from cold and running steadily (include RPM/idle stability).
Show a short clip of a load/output test (or at least alternator output if connected).
Provide compression test results (or borescope/inspection evidence).
Take close-up photos of all potential leak points (oil/coolant/fuel) and the underside/base area.
List and photograph included accessories (starter, alternator, turbo if any, injectors, cooling/radiator parts, wiring/controls) and confirm what is missing.
response.reason: The witness confirms it is a used diesel/industrial engine assembly, but the claimed Detroit 671 marine identity and working/test status are not verifiable from the provided observations. A worst-case price can be set for an unidentified used diesel engine assembly with unknown running condition, while requiring proof to raise value.
